messages.subject: DOF1 read_cross2 warnings
parts:
I am working on doing a QTL analysis of DOF1 mice (crossed with B6) and am having some difficulties with some of the downstream steps including genotype diagnostics and plotting an entire individuals contributing strains. I'm wondering if this is stemming from a warning message in the read_cross2 function which gives me 40 warnings of "In extract_dim_from_header(header) : NAs introduced by coercion"  Is this just the conversion of the second chromosome to NA for later steps? Thank you,

Justin

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] DOF1 read_cross2 warnings
parts:
With the DOF1 cross the calc_genoporb produces an array with single letter genotypes (A-H) instead of dual letter genotypes (AA-HH) so I was unsure if the NAs induces by coercion during the read_cross2 had any relation to the results produced during this step. In regards to the diagnostics, I was going through the steps to omit bad markers by looking at genotyping errors and I see about 33% of my individuals with >1% genotyping errors despite the highest percent missing genotypes at 1.1% Additionally plotting the proportion missing and proportion genotyping errors I get a graph where the majority of my markers with a high proportion of genotyping errors also are low for proportion missing. Overall I have ~4.5% of markers with >5% genotyping errors. I also cannot look for genotyping errors through the 'predict_snpgeno' method since I receive a "Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :   3 nodes produced errors; first error: incorrect number of dimensions"
I'm sorry if this information is not what you are looking for, please let me know what else I can provide. Thank you,

Justin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] DOF1 read_cross2 warnings
parts:
Maybe you could share your data files with me, privately?

The single-letter genotype labels A-H are used to save space; they shouldn't be homozygous AA-HH but rather heterozygous with all sharing some common parent, say AX, BX, ..., HX.

It sometimes helpful if you should the exact code that you used, as well as the error message.

karl
